pairs.difference: In Kabaddi a raider holds their breath and chants; in Kho Kho chasers sit in a row and tag each other in.
In Ludo you race four tokens home and can cut others; in Snakes and Ladders you climb ladders and slide down snakes.
Poker is the international game with five-card hands and chips; Teen Patti is the Indian three-card version played at Diwali parties.
Archery uses a bow and arrow; Shooting uses a gun.
High Jump is over a bar onto a mat; Long Jump is forward into a sandpit.
In Truth or Dare you pick a question or a task; in Would You Rather you choose between two options.
In Hide and Seek one player counts and the others hide; in Chor Police the teams are thieves and police, chasing.
A Marathon is 42 km of endurance; a Sprint is 100 m of pure speed.
Karate is Japanese, with punches and belts; Taekwondo is Korean, with high kicks.
In Rowing you face backwards with oars, often in a team; in Kayaking you face forwards with a double paddle.
Badminton has a shuttlecock and a high net, often played indoors; Tennis has a bouncing ball, a court and Wimbledon.
Carrom is a flat board where you flick discs with your finger; Billiards is a table where you hit balls with a cue.
Boxing means gloves and punches; Wrestling means grappling and pinning.
Hockey is played on foot; Polo is played on horseback.
In Basketball you dribble and shoot into a hoop; in Volleyball you hit the ball over a net.
Antakshari is singing songs that start with the last letter of the previous one; Dumb Charades is miming film names.
Rummy is played with a normal deck, making sets and sequences; Uno has special coloured cards, and you shout "Uno!".
Surfing rides waves on water; Skateboarding rides a board with wheels on the street.
A Javelin is a spear you throw far with a run-up; a Shot Put is a heavy ball pushed from the neck.
Formula One is cars; MotoGP is motorbikes.
Skating is on wheels or ice; Skiing is down snowy slopes with poles.
Cricket uses a bat and stumps; Football means kicking a ball into a goal.
Chess is two players moving pieces; Sudoku is a solo number puzzle.
Kite Flying is on the rooftop with manja; Marbles means flicking glass balls on the ground.
A Treasure Hunt follows clues around a place; Musical Chairs means grabbing a seat when the music stops.
In Jenga you pull blocks from a tower without toppling it; in Pictionary you draw so your team can guess the word.
Both are sports-day events. Tug of War is teams pulling a rope; a Sack Race is hopping in a sack.
Both are outdoor weekend activities. Cycling is on a bike on roads; Trekking is on foot up mountain trails.
Rock Climbing goes up a wall; Bungee Jumping falls off a bridge on a cord.
